findings.issue_text: `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5` — `z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`, no `.nonempty()`, and no uniqueness refinement. `addGuests.handler.ts:74-78` only filters guests against *existing* attendees, never against each other.

Fix: enforce in the schema — `z.array(z.string().email()).min(1).max(10).refine(uniqueCaseInsensitive)` — and de-dupe `uniqueGuests` against itself in the handler before `createMany` (or use `skipDuplicates` with a unique constraint). Add rate limiting consistent with other mutating booking endpoints.
`addGuests.handler.ts:158-165`:

Fix: build `EventManager` from the booking organizer (`booking.user` + its credentials), not `ctx.user`. Wrap the call in `try/catch` with a real logger so a calendar failure is surfaced/retried rather than producing a 500 after the DB row is already committed.

`addGuests.handler.ts:46-48` uses `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`. Since `isTeamAdmin` already returns truthy for the OWNER role, `admin && owner` collapses to `owner`, so the variable's name is a lie and every team ADMIN is denied. The `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` fallback also issues two pointless membership queries for every personal (non-team) booking.
Fix: use `||`, and short-circuit the whole block when `booking.eventType?.teamId` is nullish.
`addGuests.handler.ts` never reads `booking.eventType.disableGuests`, even though `eventType: true` is already in the include.
Fix: `if (booking.eventType?.disableGuests) throw new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", ... })`.

`packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525-548` — compare with `sendLocationChangeEmails` directly above it (`:495-523`), which gates the organizer emails on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and attendee emails on `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no `eventTypeMetadata` argument at all and sends unconditionally.

`addGuests.handler.ts:70-78`: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is lower-cased on parse but the incoming `guest` is not, so `Spammer@Blocked.com` sails past the blacklist. `.split(",")` without `.trim()` also breaks on `"a@x.com, b@y.com"`. The duplicate-attendee check `guest === attendee.email` has the same flaw — `John@X.com` will be added alongside an existing `john@x.com`.
Fix: normalize (`trim().toLowerCase()`) on both sides of both comparisons.

`addGuests.handler.ts:118-147` builds `evt` without a `team` property; `email-manager.ts:531-537` then guards on `calendarEvent.team?.members`, which is always undefined. Team hosts are never notified that guests were added to their booking. `iCalUID` and `bookerUrl` are also absent, which affects calendar matching and link generation in the templates.
Fix: populate `team` (and `iCalUID`) the way the reschedule/location handlers do, or drop the loop.

`addGuests.handler.ts:168` passes `guests`; `email-manager.ts:541` branches on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. If the caller resubmits an address that is already an attendee, that existing attendee is classified as "new" and receives a *booking-confirmed* email for a booking they already had.
Fix: pass `uniqueGuests`.

`addGuests.handler.ts:169-171`: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err` entirely and doesn't use the repo's `logger`. Email delivery failures become invisible in production — the user sees "Guests added" while nobody was notified.
Fix: `logger.error("Error sending AddGuestsEmails", safeStringify(err))`.

The handler accepts any `bookingId` regardless of `booking.status`. Guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED, or long-past bookings via the API — and via the UI too, since `bookedActions` (which contains the new menu entry) is rendered for past bookings at `apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:554`. The result is an ICS `REQUEST` with `status: "CONFIRMED"` for an event that was cancelled.
Fix: reject unless `status === ACCEPTED` (and consider rejecting past bookings), and hide the menu item accordingly.

Attendees are created with `createMany` (`addGuests.handler.ts:99-105`) with no corresponding `BookingSeat` record. For events with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, seat availability is derived from the attendee count, so this silently consumes seats and produces attendees who have no seat reference and therefore cannot cancel or manage their own seat.
Fix: either reject when `seatsPerTimeSlot` is set, or create the seat references.

`addGuests.handler.ts:55` throws with `message: "you_do_not_have_permission"`, and `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43` renders `t(err.message)`. That key does not exist anywhere in `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json` (verified — no `do_not_have_permission` / `no_permission` / `not_authorized` variants either). Users hit with a FORBIDDEN see the toast `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission`. The PR added five new keys but missed this one.

No unit test for `addGuestsHandler` (authorization matrix, blacklist, duplicate filtering, seats) and no e2e test, despite the PR adding `data-testid="add_members"`, `add-another-email`, and `add-emails` hooks that exist purely for tests. For a mutation that writes attendee rows and sends mail to arbitrary addresses, the auth and de-dup paths need real coverage.

`BookingListItem.tsx:194` gives the dropdown item `id: "add_members"` (TableActions renders `id` as the testid) and `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:98` uses the same string for the submit button. With the dialog open, a Playwright `getByTestId("add_members")` matches two elements and fails strict-mode. Rename one (and the id itself is misleading — it adds guests, not members).

**Redundant organizer query / 500 on dynamic bookings** — `addGuests.handler.ts:58-67` re-fetches the organizer even though `booking.user` was already included at `:34-39`, and `findFirstOrThrow` with `id: booking.userId || 0` throws an unhandled Prisma error (500, not a typed TRPCError) for bookings with a null `userId`.

**Client schema defined inside the render body** — `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29` rebuilds the Zod schema on every render, shadows the server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` name, and its `.refine()` has no message. Hoist it to module scope under a distinct name.

**Stale error state** — `isInvalidEmail` is reset by Cancel but not by `onSuccess` (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36-40`). Since the dialog stays mounted, reopening it after a successful add can show the red "Emails must be unique and valid" banner over an empty form.

**Dead fallback in the error toast** — `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-44`: the template literal is always truthy, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` never fires, and the toast leaks the raw tRPC code to end users.
**Silent no-op** — `handleAdd` returns without feedback when the list is empty (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49-51`); the button appears broken after the user removes the last row.

**`MultiEmail` imports from its own package barrel** — `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2` does `import { ... } from "@calcom/ui"`, while `packages/ui/index.tsx:153` re-exports `MultiEmailLazy`. That's a cycle; prefer relative imports to the concrete components.

**`MultiEmail` details** — reassigns the `value` prop (`:14`), uses `key={index}` on a removable list (`:26`), and the `<label htmlFor="emails">` (`:21`) points at no element and duplicates its id across instances (a11y). The `MultiEmailLazy.tsx:3` comment "These are like 40kb that not every user needs" is copy-pasted from `PhoneInput` and is false for a ~90-line component.
**No webhook / audit trail** — adding an attendee doesn't fire `BOOKING_UPDATED` or re-evaluate workflows, so downstream integrations never learn about the new participant.

**Recurring bookings** — guests are added to a single occurrence only; the edit menu is filtered out on the Recurring tab (`BookingListItem.tsx:246`) but is still reachable for a recurring booking from the Upcoming tab.
**Locale coverage** — new strings added to `en` only (expected if Crowdin syncs, worth confirming).

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema`) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce non-empty, maximum length, or uniqueness. In the handler, `uniqueGuests` is filtered only against existing attendees and a blacklist, but it is not de-duped against duplicates within the `guests` array itself (and comparisons are case-sensitive), so a request like `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` or `"A@x.com"` vs existing `"a@x.com"` can result in duplicate attendee rows via `createMany`. This is a real correctness/data-integrity issue introduced by the diff. The rate-limiting and specific max(10) are additional recommendations not strictly verifiable from the diff, but the core schema/handler validation gaps are real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `addGuests.handler.ts:158-165`:

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the code filters the requested emails into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only persists those. However, near the end (around lines 158-165) it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the original `guests` input rather than `uniqueGuests`. Since `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the provided list to decide which attendees are “new” (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))`), passing the unfiltered list can misclassify existing attendees as “new” and send them the wrong email type. This is a concrete correctness bug introduced by the diff because `uniqueGuests` is computed but not used for the email logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fix: build `EventManager` from the booking organizer (`booking.user` + its credentials), not `ctx.user`. Wrap the call in `try/catch` with a real logger so a calendar failure is surfaced/retried rather than producing a 500 after the DB row is already committed.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller). But this mutation is explicitly allowed for non-organizers (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner), so the caller may not be the booking organizer and may not have the organizer’s calendar credentials. That makes `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` likely to fail or update the wrong calendar when someone other than the organizer adds guests. Additionally, `prisma.booking.update(...)` commits the new attendees before `updateCalendarAttendees` runs, and that call is not wrapped in `try/catch`; if it throws, the request errors after the DB is updated, leaving DB and external calendar out of sync. The diff already shows they only catch email-sending errors, not calendar update errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fix: normalize (`trim().toLowerCase()`) on both sides of both comparisons.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, duplicate/blacklist checks are case-sensitive and don’t normalize inputs:
- `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` will treat `User@Example.com` as different from `user@example.com`.
- `blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased, but the code checks `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so uppercase variants bypass the blacklist.
Additionally, the dialog-side uniqueness refine uses `new Set(emails)` which is also case-sensitive. Normalizing via `trim().toLowerCase()` on both sides would prevent these correctness/security bypasses.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the constructed CalendarEvent `evt` includes organizer/attendees/etc but no `team` field (nor any team members). In sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts) it formats the event and then only notifies additional hosts via `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... }`. With `evt` lacking `team`, that branch will not run, so team members beyond the main organizer will not be emailed from this code path. However, the claim about missing `iCalUID` is not supported by the diff because `evt.uid` is set, and the `bookerUrl` impact is speculative without seeing template requirements.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fix: populate `team` (and `iCalUID`) the way the reschedule/location handlers do, or drop the loop.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `sendAddGuestsEmails()` explicitly tries to email all `calendarEvent.team.members` (it has a loop guarded by `if (calendarEvent.team?.members)`). But in the new `addGuestsHandler` the constructed `evt: CalendarEvent` does not populate `team` at all (only `organizer`, `attendees`, `uid`, etc.). As a result, for team bookings, that loop will never run and team members will not receive the organizer notification email, despite the code being written to do so. The proposed fix (populate `team` similarly to other handlers or remove the loop) addresses this concrete mismatch introduced in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code computes `uniqueGuests` (filtered to exclude existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only adds those to the booking via `createMany`. But it then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passing the original `guests` array, not `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` determines whether an attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (treated as a newly added guest) vs an update email (`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`). Passing `guests` can incorrectly classify existing attendees (or otherwise not-added emails) as “new”, causing wrong email type/content to be sent. The correct list to pass is the actually-added guests, i.e. `uniqueGuests` (ideally also de-duped).

The proposed fix also references `logger` and `safeStringify(err)`, neither of which exist/import in the diff, so it’s not a verifiable issue with the current changes—more of a logging/style preference.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the booking is fetched with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and then updated to add attendees, but there is no check of any booking lifecycle field (e.g., `booking.status`, `booking.cancelled`, `booking.endTime` vs now, etc.) before mutating. This means that if a user is authorized (organizer/attendee/team admin/owner), they can add guests to any booking record regardless of whether it is cancelled/rejected/past. Additionally, the emails/ICS generated in the new email templates hardcode `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"`, so if the underlying booking was cancelled, the outgoing ICS would contradict that state. The specific claim about the UI rendering this action for past bookings at a particular line number isn’t verifiable from the provided diff hunk, but the lack of server-side status validation and the CONFIRMED ICS are directly observable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fix: reject unless `status === ACCEPTED` (and consider rejecting past bookings), and hide the menu item accordingly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an “Add guests” menu item and a new `addGuests` mutation/handler, but nowhere in the shown changes is there a `status` field on `booking` being read or written, nor any logic that implies bookings must be `ACCEPTED` before allowing guest changes. The handler fetches the booking and checks permissions (team admin/owner, organizer, attendee) and then updates attendees regardless of time/status; however, whether that’s incorrect depends on product rules not present in the diff. Because the proposed finding hinges on a specific `status === ACCEPTED` requirement and UI hiding logic that is not evidenced by the diff, it is speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendees are created with `createMany` (`addGuests.handler.ts:99-105`) with no corresponding `BookingSeat` record. For events with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, seat availability is derived from the attendee count, so this silently consumes seats and produces attendees who have no seat reference and therefore cannot cancel or manage their own seat.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds guests by inserting new `attendees` rows via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and does not reference any `BookingSeat` model/table or seat-management API. The proposed finding assumes (1) a `BookingSeat` record must exist per attendee for seat-based events and (2) seat availability/cancellation flows depend on that relationship. Neither assumption is verifiable from the diff itself. From what is shown, creating attendees without additional seat records could be the intended representation (i.e., attendees *are* the seats), so the claim that it “silently consumes seats” or makes attendees unable to manage seats is speculative given the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fix: either reject when `seatsPerTimeSlot` is set, or create the seat references.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation blindly `createMany` attendees for a booking without checking `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or current attendee count) and without creating any seat-related records. Yet the code explicitly propagates `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` into the `CalendarEvent` (`evt.seatsPerTimeSlot = booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`), indicating the system supports seat-limited bookings. As written, this can oversubscribe a seated booking and/or leave seat-based state inconsistent (attendees added with no corresponding seat allocation), which is a concrete correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `addGuests.handler.ts:55` throws with `message: "you_do_not_have_permission"`, and `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43` renders `t(err.message)`. That key does not exist anywhere in `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json` (verified — no `do_not_have_permission` / `no_permission` / `not_authorized` variants either). Users hit with a FORBIDDEN see the toast `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission`. The PR added five new keys but missed this one.

adjudication.rationale: The new handler does throw `new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" })` and the new dialog formats errors as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. However, the claim that `you_do_not_have_permission` is missing from `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json` is not verifiable from this diff: only small portions of `common.json` are shown, not the full file, so we cannot conclude the key does not exist elsewhere in that file (or other loaded namespaces). Therefore the finding relies on information not provable from the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unit test for `addGuestsHandler` (authorization matrix, blacklist, duplicate filtering, seats) and no e2e test, despite the PR adding `data-testid="add_members"`, `add-another-email`, and `add-emails` hooks that exist purely for tests. For a mutation that writes attendee rows and sends mail to arbitrary addresses, the auth and de-dup paths need real coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new functionality (addGuests TRPC mutation, dialog UI, and data-testid hooks), but it does not show any tests being added. However, the proposed finding asserts there are no unit/e2e tests for this behavior, which is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone (tests could exist elsewhere outside the shown changes). Additionally, “missing tests” is a quality/process concern rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness defect that can be proven from the code change itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `BookingListItem.tsx:194` gives the dropdown item `id: "add_members"` (TableActions renders `id` as the testid) and `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:98` uses the same string for the submit button. With the dialog open, a Playwright `getByTestId("add_members")` matches two elements and fails strict-mode. Rename one (and the id itself is misleading — it adds guests, not members).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce the same literal string "add_members" in two places: the new table action item in `BookingListItem.tsx` (`id: "add_members"`) and the submit button in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` (`data-testid="add_members"`). However, the finding’s claim that this definitively causes a Playwright strict-mode failure depends on behavior not shown in the diff: that `TableActions` renders the action `id` as a `data-testid`, and that the dropdown item remains in the DOM when the dialog is open. Neither is verifiable from the provided changes, so the failure is plausible but not a confirmed defect strictly attributable to this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Redundant organizer query / 500 on dynamic bookings** — `addGuests.handler.ts:58-67` re-fetches the organizer even though `booking.user` was already included at `:34-39`, and `findFirstOrThrow` with `id: booking.userId || 0` throws an unhandled Prisma error (500, not a typed TRPCError) for bookings with a null `userId`.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst({ include: { user: { include: ... }}})` already loads the related `booking.user` object, so the subsequent organizer lookup is redundant from a data-fetch perspective. More importantly, the code does `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 }})`: if `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined`, it will query `id = 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma “record not found” error (not a `TRPCError`), which will propagate as an internal/500-style error rather than a typed TRPC error. The use of `booking.userId || 0` suggests the author expects `userId` may be nullable, making this a real, verifiable risk in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Client schema defined inside the render body** — `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29` rebuilds the Zod schema on every render, shadows the server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` name, and its `.refine()` has no message. Hoist it to module scope under a distinct name.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the Zod schema (`const ZAddGuestsInputSchema = ...`) is indeed created inside the component function, so it will be re-instantiated on each render. However, this is primarily a minor performance/style concern, not a clear correctness/bug/security defect. It also does not actually “shadow” the server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in any verifiable way in this diff because the client file does not import the server schema; the name collision is only conceptual across files. Finally, the `.refine()` lacking a custom message is not a defect here because the code doesn’t consume Zod’s error message; it just toggles `isInvalidEmail` and shows a fixed translated string (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Stale error state** — `isInvalidEmail` is reset by Cancel but not by `onSuccess` (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36-40`). Since the dialog stays mounted, reopening it after a successful add can show the red "Emails must be unique and valid" banner over an empty form.

adjudication.rationale: `AddGuestsDialog` keeps `isInvalidEmail` in component state and the component is always mounted from `BookingListItem` (it’s just toggled via `Dialog open={isOpenDialog}`). `handleAdd()` sets `isInvalidEmail(true)` on failed validation, but neither `handleAdd()` (on a subsequent successful submit) nor the mutation `onSuccess` resets it. `onSuccess` closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` to `[""]`, but leaves `isInvalidEmail` untouched, so reopening the dialog can still render the red error banner even with an empty/reset form.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Dead fallback in the error toast** — `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-44`: the template literal is always truthy, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` never fires, and the toast leaks the raw tRPC code to end users.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a (non-empty) string because template literals coerce `undefined` to the string "undefined" and still include the colon/space. Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never hit the fallback. Additionally, the toast will display the raw `err.data?.code` (e.g., TRPC error codes) to end users, which matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Silent no-op** — `handleAdd` returns without feedback when the list is empty (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49-51`); the button appears broken after the user removes the last row.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.handleAdd`, when `multiEmailValue.length === 0` it immediately `return`s with no toast/error state update. This empty-array state is reachable: `MultiEmail`’s remove (“x”) handler `splice`s the array, so removing the last row makes `value` become `[]`. When that happens, `MultiEmail` switches to rendering an “Add Emails” button (no rows), but the dialog footer still shows the primary “Add” button; clicking it triggers `handleAdd` and results in no visible feedback (silent no-op), making the button appear broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`MultiEmail` imports from its own package barrel** — `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2` does `import { ... } from "@calcom/ui"`, while `packages/ui/index.tsx:153` re-exports `MultiEmailLazy`. That's a cycle; prefer relative imports to the concrete components.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` the component imports UI primitives from the package barrel (`import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui";`). The barrel (`packages/ui/index.tsx`) now re-exports `MultiEmail` via `./form/MultiEmailLazy`, and `MultiEmailLazy` dynamically imports `./MultiEmail`. This creates a verifiable circular dependency chain: `MultiEmail.tsx -> @calcom/ui (index.tsx) -> MultiEmailLazy.tsx -> import("./MultiEmail") -> MultiEmail.tsx`. Even though the last edge is dynamic, the cycle is present in the module graph and is the kind of defect that can cause initialization-order/runtime bundling issues and should be avoided by using relative imports to the concrete primitive modules instead of the barrel from within the same package.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`MultiEmail` details** — reassigns the `value` prop (`:14`), uses `key={index}` on a removable list (`:26`), and the `<label htmlFor="emails">` (`:21`) points at no element and duplicates its id across instances (a11y). The `MultiEmailLazy.tsx:3` comment "These are like 40kb that not every user needs" is copy-pasted from `PhoneInput` and is false for a ~90-line component.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the code uses `<label htmlFor="emails">` but none of the rendered inputs are given `id="emails"` (the `EmailField` instances do not receive an `id` prop), so the label is not programmatically associated with a control (a11y defect) and would be wrong across multiple instances as well. Also, the list is rendered with `key={index}` while items can be removed via `splice`, which is a known React correctness issue that can cause inputs to keep the wrong internal state after deletions/reorders. Reassigning `value` (`value = value || []`) and the "40kb" comment are more nits, but the label/keys issues are real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **No webhook / audit trail** — adding an attendee doesn't fire `BOOKING_UPDATED` or re-evaluate workflows, so downstream integrations never learn about the new participant.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` flow (`addGuests.handler.ts`) updates the booking’s `attendees`, updates the external calendar via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and sends emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails`, but it does not emit any webhook/event like `BOOKING_UPDATED` in the shown diff. However, the finding asserts a specific contract (“should fire BOOKING_UPDATED / re-evaluate workflows so downstream integrations learn”) that is not established anywhere in the diff (no existing webhook mechanism or expected behavior is shown for booking mutations such as `editLocation`). Without that contextual contract in the changed code, this is not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.
